title: v0.3.3: enforce the dispersion-doc sync and extras resolution in CI
body:
Turns two documented-but-unenforced invariants into tests. **No runtime behavior changes.**

## 1. `dispersion.py` ↔ `docs/models.md` drift is now caught

`dispersion.py` states its table "MUST be kept in sync" with `docs/models.md`, and AGENTS.md invariant 4 repeats it. Nothing verified it. That document is the only place a reader learns *why* a model refuses `dispersion=True` — drift there is a chemistry documentation bug, the kind that gets copied into a methods section.

`tests/test_models_doc_sync.py` parses the table and compares it against `_POLICIES` in both directions:

- every policy entry has a documented row,
- every documented row has a policy entry,
- the ⛔/✅ verdict matches `includes_dispersion`, and the `xc=` matches `d3_xc` for every allowed row.

The two directions matter separately: a missing row hides behavior, an extra row promises behavior the code does not implement.

Verified against injected drift rather than assumed to work — flipping `spice` from refused to allowed, and changing `pet_mad`'s documented `xc` from `pbesol` to `pbe`, each fail the expected test:

```
E   assert False == True
E   assert 'pbe' == 'pbesol'
FAILED test_documented_verdict_matches_the_policy[sevennet-spice]
FAILED test_documented_verdict_matches_the_policy[sevennet-pet_mad]
```

The table's first column now names every policy key in backticks (`default`, `1M`/`5M`, `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), which is what the parser reads and is more consistent regardless.

## 2. CI resolves every extra on every supported Python

The fast suite mocks every NNP backend, which keeps it quick but means **nothing checked that the extras can still be installed**. An upstream cap or conflict stayed invisible until a user hit it — the `uma`/Python 3.14 incompatibility that shipped in 0.3.2 was found by hand, not by CI.

The new `extras-resolve` job resolves all 7 extras against all 3 supported Pythons with `uv pip compile`. Resolution only: no wheels downloaded, nothing installed, and `--python-version` resolves for an interpreter that is not present. 21 combinations in seconds.

Its expectations mirror the README support table, so it fails in **both** directions — when an extra stops resolving, and when one documented as unavailable starts working. The second case is the interesting one: when fairchem-core gains 3.14 support, CI turns red telling us the docs are now pessimistic.

Run locally against this branch:

```
py3.12 [chgnet]: resolves      py3.13 [chgnet]: resolves      py3.14 [chgnet]: resolves
py3.12 [sevennet]: resolves    py3.13 [sevennet]: resolves    py3.14 [sevennet]: resolves
py3.12 [mattersim]: resolves   py3.13 [mattersim]: resolves   py3.14 [mattersim]: resolves
py3.12 [nequip]: resolves      py3.13 [nequip]: resolves      py3.14 [nequip]: resolves
py3.12 [uma]: resolves         py3.13 [uma]: resolves         py3.14 [uma]: fails
py3.12 [dispersion]: resolves  py3.13 [dispersion]: resolves  py3.14 [dispersion]: resolves
py3.12 [all]: resolves         py3.13 [all]: resolves         py3.14 [all]: fails
EXIT=0
```

## 3. `docs/code-guide_ja.md`: molecular charge and spin

The guide had nothing on the most backend-dependent behavior in the package. Adds which backend accepts charge/spin, that UMA silently falls back to a neutral singlet when they are missing, and why `get_calculator` deliberately has no `charge=`/`spin=` keyword.

## Not in this PR

Exercising the seven newly documented SevenNet modals (`spice`, `qcml`, `pet_mad`, `mp_r2scan`, `odac23`, `oc20`, `oc22`) in the `slow` suite. Those need real model weights (GBs) and are still unverified against a running model — tracked separately.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` on 3.13 — 132 passed, 22 deselected
- [x] `pytest` on 3.14.6 — 132 passed, 22 deselected
- [x] doc-sync test fails on injected drift (both verdict and `xc`)
- [x] `extras-resolve` script run locally — 21/21 as expected, exit 0
- [x] `ruff check src tests examples`
- [ ] CI

title: v0.3.2: support Python 3.14 and publish to PyPI
body:
Prepares the first PyPI release.

## Drop the `requires-python` upper bound

`requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.14"` becomes `">=3.12"`.

An upper cap is written into the metadata of every file uploaded to PyPI and cannot be edited afterwards — lifting it needs a whole new release. With `<3.14` in place, a Python 3.14 user running `pip install ase-calculator-kit` is told no version satisfies the requirement: the package does not look outdated, it looks nonexistent. Python 3.14 was released 2025-10-07 and is now at 3.14.6.

Verified rather than assumed:

- The full fast suite passes on **3.14.6** with ase 3.29.0 (98 passed).
- `chgnet`, `sevennet`, `mattersim`, `nequip`, and `torch-dftd` all resolve on 3.14.
- CI matrix extended to `["3.12", "3.13", "3.14"]`.

## `uma` on 3.14, and why there is no environment marker

`fairchem-core` declares `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` and pins `torch~=2.8.0`, which ships no cp314 wheels. So on 3.14:

| | 3.12 | 3.13 | 3.14 |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Core, `chgnet`, `sevennet`, `mattersim`, `nequip`, `dispersion` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `uma`, and therefore `all` | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |

The `uma` extra is left **unmarked** on purpose. A `; python_version < "3.14"` marker would make `pip install "ase-calculator-kit[uma]"` *succeed* on 3.14 with no UMA installed — the user finds out at `get_calculator("uma")`, receiving a `MissingDependencyError` telling them to install an extra they did install. Bare, pip fails immediately with an error naming `fairchem-core`, so the cause and the owner of the fix are both obvious. Nothing here changes once fairchem-core supports 3.14.

New AGENTS.md invariant 10 records this, and `tests/test_packaging.py` now fails if a cap reappears.

## Also

Fixes a stale README claim — inherited with the API-reference commit in #2 — that SevenNet ships as a base dependency. The default install has been ASE + PyYAML only since 0.3.0.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` on 3.13 — 98 passed, 22 deselected
- [x] `pytest` on 3.14.6 — 98 passed, 22 deselected
- [x] `ruff check src tests examples`
- [x] `python -m build` + `twine check` — both artifacts PASSED
- [ ] CI on 3.12 / 3.13 / 3.14

After merge: tag `v0.3.2` and publish to PyPI via the `release.yml` manual dispatch (the pending publisher is registered).

title: v0.3.1: correct the molecular-task chemistry, and land PR #1 without the SevenNet base dependency
body:
## Summary

Two things, released together as **v0.3.1**.

**1. The parts of #1 that are not the SevenNet dependency change.** Three commits are cherry-picked as-is, keeping @atsushi-ishikawa as author: the sevenn debug-print suppression, the README API reference + `AGENTS.md`, and the PyPI packaging prep (ranges + `constraints.txt`, PEP 639 license, `py.typed`, classifiers, release workflow). The two commits that promote `sevenn` to a base dependency are **not** taken — the 0.3.0 "lightweight default" decision stands, so a bare `pip install ase-calculator-kit` still does not pull in torch. `AGENTS.md` invariant 9 is rewritten accordingly, and the CI comment stays truthful.

`release.yml` is adjusted so a `v*` tag only builds and version-checks. Uploading is a manual `workflow_dispatch`, because PyPI Trusted Publishing is not configured yet and this package is not on PyPI — a tag must not turn the workflow red.

**2. An audit of the molecular tasks (`uma` `omol`, `7net-omni` `omol25_*`, and the rest), which found real errors.**

### `omol25_low` was documented wrong

It was described as "molecular / high-fidelity molecular systems". It is the **low-spin** OMol25 task, the counterpart of the high-spin `omol25_high`. Both are ωB97M-V; the split is by spin state, not accuracy. Seven further `7net-omni` tasks (`mp_r2scan`, `oc20`, `oc22`, `odac23`, `spice`, `qcml`, `pet_mad`) were undocumented, which also kept them off the dispersion table.

### Four molecular tasks could have double-counted dispersion

Anything absent from the policy table lands on the "unverified" tier, which is *overridable* with an explicit `dispersion_xc=`. That is the right default for an unknown materials task, but molecular reference data is nearly always dispersion-corrected, so it was the wrong place for these. Each was verified against its dataset's primary source and moved to the always-refused tier:

| Task | Reference level | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| SevenNet `spice` | ωB97M-**D3(BJ)**/def2-TZVPPD | unverified (overridable) | ⛔ always refused |
| SevenNet `qcml` | PBE0 + **MBD-NL** | unverified (overridable) | ⛔ always refused |
| SevenNet `odac23` | **PBE-D3** | unverified (overridable) | ⛔ always refused |
| UMA `odac` | **PBE-D3** (ODAC23) | unverified (overridable) | ⛔ always refused |
| UMA `omc` | **PBE+D3** (OMC25) | unverified (overridable) | ⛔ always refused |

Newly allowed with a verified functional: `mp_r2scan` (D3 `xc=r2scan`) and `pet_mad` (D3 `xc=pbesol`). `omat24`/`oc22` are relabelled PBE(+U) to match SevenNet's own table; their D3 `xc` is unchanged.

No row is left unverified. The tier stays for tasks upstream adds later, and a test pins that molecular tasks never sit on it.

**Behaviour change:** `get_calculator("uma", task="odac", dispersion=True, dispersion_xc="pbe")` used to work and now raises `DispersionError`. That call was double-counting D3, so the raise is the fix. The README example that used it has been replaced.

### Charge and spin behave differently per backend, and neither was documented properly

- **sevenn has no charge or spin input at all** (`charge` does not appear anywhere in sevenn 0.12.1). Its molecular modals cannot express an ion or a chosen open-shell state — the modal embedding is the only handle.
- **UMA can, but does not enforce it.** `validate_atoms_data()` does not raise on a missing `charge`/`spin`: it logs a warning, writes `charge=0` / `spin=1` into the `atoms.info` dict the caller passed in, and returns a neutral closed-shell result. An anion or a radical therefore comes back **silently wrong**.

New README section "Molecular systems (charge and spin)" covers both, with OH⁻ and OH-radical examples, and notes the non-periodic cell behaviour. `examples/run_all_models.py` now exercises every documented SevenNet modal plus those two ions.

No runtime API changed for charge/spin — a `charge=`/`spin=` keyword on `get_calculator` would have to be silently dropped for SevenNet, which is worse than not offering it. A test pins that.

## Not included: OrbMol

Adding an OrbMol backend was the original goal and is **deferred**. `orb-models` 0.7.0 hard-pins `dm-tree==0.1.8`, which has no cp313 wheel on any platform, so it cannot be installed on Python 3.13 — one of the two versions this project supports and tests. (There is no *version* conflict: all backends plus orb-models resolve together cleanly, converging on torch 2.8.0.) Worth revisiting when upstream relaxes that pin.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest` — 97 passed, 22 deselected (3.13, local)
- [x] `ruff check src tests examples`
- [x] `python -m build` — sdist and wheel build as 0.3.1
- [ ] CI on 3.12 / 3.13

Closes #1.

title: Ship SevenNet by default, quiet its debug prints, and document the API
body:
## Summary

- **SevenNet installed by default** (v0.3.1): `sevenn==0.12.1` moves from the `sevennet` extra into the base dependencies, so `pip install ase-calculator-kit` gives a working NNP backend out of the box. The `sevennet` extra is kept as a no-op alias so existing `ase-calculator-kit[sevennet]` installs keep resolving. Note this pulls torch into the default install, partially reversing the 0.3.0 "lightweight default" decision.
- **Quiet SevenNet construction**: sevenn 0.12.1 unconditionally prints `cueq` / `<bool>` / `flash` / `<bool>` from `SevenNetCalculator.__init__` (`sevenn/calculator.py:83-86`). The backend now filters exactly those pairs while the calculator is built and forwards any other stdout from the model load.
- **Documentation for humans and AI agents**: new README API Reference (calculator names + aliases, per-backend keywords with defaults, the DFT three-keyword contract, exception table), a note that `dispersion=True` returns a `SumCalculator`, removal of the `.venv/bin/...` command prefixes that get copied into environments without a `.venv`, and a new `AGENTS.md` holding the repository map, design invariants, conventions, and known upstream quirks.
- **CI comment** corrected: the fast-test job now installs torch via sevenn, contrary to what it claimed.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI fast suite on Python 3.12 / 3.13 + `ruff check`

pytest was not available in the authoring environment, so `test_sevennet_debug_prints_are_suppressed` and the updated `tests/test_packaging.py` assertions have **not** been run locally — CI is their first execution. The suppression logic itself was verified end to end with a standalone script using a fake noisy `sevenn.calculator` module (captured stdout was exactly `Loading 7net-omni\n`), and the packaging metadata assertions were checked directly with `tomllib`.
